reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: Two Paper Hall tickets on 2025-01-22 share site, day and run, and the January scale export stores one summed cell for that site-day.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The customer review states that separate tickets on the same day remain separate rows; the tickets have distinct references WT-GL-PH-JAN-F6A and WT-GL-PH-JAN-F6B and distinct raw masses 11.997 kg and 11.527 kg.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The January scale-export weights sheet has a single Paper Hall cell on 2025-01-22 of 23.524 kg and containers 2, which equals 11.997+11.527.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The cell is an export sum, not a third visit; the two tickets remain separate collection stops. Merging them into the cell would drop ticket identity.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The weigh-ticket index states it is derived from the same event table as the collection register.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The index is a different document with its own transcription note (Station House containers 3) and attachment flags; collapsing it into the register would drop those assertions.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The 2025-08-22 note copies the 2025-05-19 worksheet balances.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The note is a later reconstruction that also asserts the absence of a bank statement and an internal request to separate delay charges; the worksheet has VAT, day-counts and due dates the note does not repeat as its own snapshot.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The certificate says it carries the period total from the customer review, and both name GL-CERT-JTS-R4A's window.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: They are different issuances: the certificate is a corrected signed reissue with 20.415 t and 3761 Nm³; the review also publishes 20.405 t and 3763 Nm³ on page 4.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The account card repeats term, rates and notice periods of the signed agreement.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The card is an internal reading dated 2025-08-21, not the signed instrument, and itself says it records the team's reading of the papers.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: Both are the only ticket forms in the packet and both name collector Henry Wilson and carrier GreenLoop.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: They are different dates, sites, statuses (final weighed vs provisional tare-only) and runs.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: Both occur on 2025-02-05 in the Hearth naming family.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: One is the unassigned Hearth label with no site_code; the other is Hearth counter SITE-HS. The review says the unassigned label keeps its original fields.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The spelling Mill Rd. is an alias of Mill Road on some 2025 tickets that also carry SITE-MR.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: The 2024-02 CSV row labelled Mill Rd. has no site_code and no counts; treating it as a Mill Road process month would invent collections the row does not record.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: The two files are byte-identical and the manifest records them as representations of one source.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: Creating a second set of 285 visit situations from the copy would duplicate every 2025 stop; the copy is not an independent operational record.

reversibility_cases.why_they_might_be_merged: Both are Hearth office tickets in January with a numeric raw field.
reversibility_cases.why_that_would_be_wrong: 2025-01-01 is an empty return with containers 0 and net zero recorded; 2025-01-08 is a weighed visit with containers 1. Zero recorded is not a weighed mass of contents.
